source: Current ChatGPT conversation, How Transformer works, cards 01–15, including partial and final continuations.

manifest.title: 01 · Tokenization
manifest.explanation: The sentence is split into tokens. Each token receives a numerical ID from the tokenizer's vocabulary.

manifest.title: 02 · Embedding lookup
manifest.explanation: The ID selects a learned vector containing numerical features. Real Transformers typically use hundreds or thousands of dimensions.

manifest.title: 03 · Positional information
manifest.explanation: Position matters. Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), for example, rotate query and key vector components according to token position.

manifest.title: 04 · Query, Key and Value
manifest.explanation: Three learned weight matrices transform each token representation into a Query, Key and Value vector.

manifest.title: 05 · Attention scores
manifest.explanation: Each query is compared with every key using a dot product. Higher scores indicate stronger attention compatibility.

manifest.title: 06 · Causal masking
manifest.explanation: A GPT-style Transformer cannot look at future tokens. Masked attention scores become negative infinity before softmax.

manifest.title: 07 · Softmax normalization
manifest.explanation: Softmax converts the scores into attention weights that add up to 100%. Here, the token “cat” receives the most attention.

manifest.title: 08 · Combining value vectors
manifest.explanation: Every value vector is multiplied by its attention weight. Their weighted sum creates a new context-aware representation.

manifest.title: 09 · Multi-head attention
manifest.explanation: Multiple attention heads work in parallel using different learned projections, allowing the model to capture different contextual relationships.

manifest.title: 10 · Head concatenation & projection
manifest.explanation: Head outputs are joined and multiplied by a learned output matrix to produce one unified representation.

manifest.title: 11 · Residual connection & normalization
manifest.explanation: Normalization stabilizes computation. The residual connection adds the attention result to the original representation. Shown here is the pre-normalization design.

manifest.title: 12 · Feed-forward network
manifest.explanation: Each token independently passes through a neural network that expands its dimensions, applies a nonlinear transformation and projects it back.

manifest.title: 13 · Stacking Transformer blocks
manifest.explanation: Attention, feed-forward networks, normalization and residual connections repeat across many layers, progressively transforming the token representations.

manifest.title: 14 · Language modeling head
manifest.explanation: The final representation is projected into vocabulary-sized logits. Softmax produces next-token probabilities, and a decoding strategy selects a token.

manifest.title: 15 · Autoregressive generation
manifest.explanation: Each generated token becomes part of the context for predicting the next token. This process repeats until a stopping condition is reached.
